issues: src/lib/validation.ts validateBackupPassphrase uses `p.length < 11`, which is off-by-one from the spec ("at least 12 characters"). This means an 11-character passphrase like '12345678901' is incorrectly accepted (confirmed by direct execution: validateBackupPassphrase('12345678901') returns null, not an error). The existing passphraseRules.test.ts test happens to pass only because its 'exactly12!!' test string is actually 11 characters long (a bug in the test itself), masking this defect. Fix the validation to require length >= 12 (i.e. `if (p.length < 12) return ...`), and correct the test to use a genuinely 12+ character string so the boundary is actually exercised. This is a real functional defect: the task explicitly requires 'at least 12 characters' and the current code permits an 11-character passphrase to create a backup, which also means encrypted backups could be created with weaker-than-specified protection.
feedback: All other hardening items (encryption-key purge on delete-all-data with policy preserved, backup temp-file cleanup, File API usage for photos with bytes()/write(), numeric validation helpers and UI wiring, backup structure validation before restore mutates data, export button disabling) look correctly implemented and are covered by passing unit/acceptance tests. However, the backup passphrase minimum-length check is off by one (uses `< 11` instead of `< 12`), so an 11-character passphrase is wrongly accepted, violating requirement (3). The existing test for this (passphraseRules.test.ts) doesn't catch it because its 'valid' example string is also only 11 characters. Please fix the boundary condition in validateBackupPassphrase and update/add a test with a correctly-counted 12-character string to verify the boundary properly.
